title: Meet a New Classmate
objective: Hold a 6-8 turn introduction conversation: greet, names, origin, job, close.
intro_md: [L1: Today you put Unit 1 together: you meet a new classmate. First you rebuild the conversation in parts — greet, names, where from, jobs, goodbye. Then you do it for real with the AI, first in writing at your own speed, then speaking, 6-8 turns. If you don't understand something, use Sorry? or Can you repeat that, please? — that is always good English and it counts in your favor.]
notes: TODO_audio: exercise 6 needs recorded audio; the quoted text stands in for the recording. Integration lesson — band map allocates 0 new vocabulary; everything recycles L01-L15. Written interaction (ex 8) precedes the spoken one (ex 9) per the band's structured-to-guided progression.

exercises.prompt: hello · What's your name? · Where are you from? · What do you do? · Nice to meet you. · see you later
exercises.rationale: Retrieval sweep of the five conversational moves before assembly — FSRS retrieval right before use maximizes the dialogue's success rate.

exercises.prompt: [L1: Every conversation has parts. Match each sentence to its job in the conversation.]

pairs.right: [L1: opening: greet and give your name]

exercises.rationale: Names the functional skeleton (greet, ask, answer, close) so the later dialogue is a plan the learner executes, not a memory test.

exercises.prompt: [L1: Put the four lines in order to build the opening of the conversation.]
exercises.key: Hello! I'm Dan. Hi! My name is Eva. Nice to meet you. Nice to meet you, too.
exercises.rationale: Sequencing adjacency pairs (greeting answers greeting, name answers name, Nice-to-meet-you gets a too) — conversation structure, not sentence grammar, is the target.

exercises.prompt: [L1: Match each question to a good answer.]
exercises.rationale: The four question chunks are the learner's whole turn inventory; answering the wrong frame (giving a job for an origin question) is the most common breakdown in the live dialogue.

exercises.prompt: A: Hi! I'm Leo. What's your ___?  B: My name is Ana.  A: Where are you ___?  B: I'm from Mexico. What do you ___?  A: I'm a driver.
exercises.rationale: The full model script with its frame words removed — completing it is controlled dialogue completion in miniature (the band's written U1 interaction type); distractors are the word-for-word template errors ('Where are you country?').

exercises.prompt: [audio, 1.0x] 'Hi! I'm Nina. I'm from Brazil. I'm a nurse.' — [L1: What is her job?]
exercises.rationale: Three I'm-sentences in a row do three different things (name, origin, job); listeners must track which frame carries the answer, not just catch I'm.

options.label: She's a nurse.
options.rationale: After 'I'm a' comes the job — the third frame answers the question.

options.label: She's from Brazil.
options.rationale: That is her country: 'I'm from' is the origin frame, not the job frame.

options.label: Her name is Nina.
options.rationale: That is the name frame — plain 'I'm' plus a name, no 'a', no 'from'.

exercises.prompt: A: I'm from Vancouver.  B: ___? Can you repeat that, please?
exercises.rationale: Inserts the L15 repair move into the introduction script exactly where it will be needed live; repair is an always-permitted, positively scored move in the next two exercises.

exercises.prompt: [L1: Written chat, your speed. The AI classmate writes a greeting and questions. Answer in full sentences — then ask the same question back.]
exercises.rationale: Controlled written completion before real-time speech (band progression: controlled dialogue completion precedes guided Q&A); asking the question back trains initiative, the skill that separates L17 from every earlier dialogue.

exercises.prompt: [L1: Now speak. Meet your new AI classmate: 6-8 turns. Greet, exchange names, say where you are from, ask about jobs, and close the conversation. Use your repair phrases any time you need them.]
exercises.rationale: The lesson's target performance: scripted-then-flexed integration of L01/L03/L05/L06/L13 chunks in real time, sustaining 6-8 turns; counts toward guided-interaction minutes and rehearses the L18 mission.
